title: Schema-fidelity scoring and rollback triggers for model/config rollouts
creator: Ava Patel
description: Build a lightweight, deploy-time and runtime scoring system that quantifies schema fidelity per-response and aggregates field-level risk scores to drive automated rollback or alerting during model and config rollouts. This covers both strict JSON schema violations and semantic 'near-miss' mismatches (e.g., type coercions, enum drift, nested field truncation). The goal is to give rollouts a measurable fidelity signal tied to config deltas so we can automatically pause/rollback a rollout or open a prioritized incident with suggested remediation hints.
acceptance_criteria: Per-response schema-fidelity score emitted to Observability with <=5ms overhead on p95 path
Field-level delta attribution report available in Console for every rollout with top-5 contributing fields
Automatic rollback trigger rule: fidelity drop > 8 percentage points vs baseline over 10k samples within a 5 minute window
Alert payload includes suggested remediation: 'revert config X', 'pin model to vY', or 'increase kv_cache size' where applicable
Integration tests in eval-harness that injects controlled schema perturbations and validates rollback behavior
implementation_notes: Prototype scoreer implemented as a small Rust module that runs inside the serving runtime and emits a compact fidelity vector
Score combines deterministic schema checks (jsonschema) with a fuzzy-field matcher that allows tolerated variants (string/number coercion rules configurable per-field)
Aggregate signal exported via existing tracing pipeline and a new lightweight metric 'schema_fidelity.p95'
Console will render a per-rollout heatmap and suggest the top 3 remediation actions using a simple rule engine (config deltas -> likely root cause)
We will gate the auto-rollback feature behind a 'safety.rollout.rollback' feature flag scoped per-customer
comments: 2026-02-20 - Ava Patel: Created ticket to formalize prototype work from spike. Spike showed detectable near-miss drift for enum fields when switching tokenizer and a config that enabled 'compact-objects'.

2026-02-25 - Diego Morales: Spike PR opened: github.com/redwood/serving/pull/8923. Initial Rust scorer emits per-field 'ok'|'warning'|'error' and a numeric fidelity score. Measured overhead ~3ms median on local GPU dev box.

2026-03-02 - PM review (Jordan Lee): Requested explicit remediation mappings for the most common remediation actions — added mapping work to implementation Notes. Also asked for a canary run plan and SLO changes during experiment.

2026-03-05 - Design feedback (Priya Nair): Console heatmap should include sample-level drilldown and a compact diff view showing the failing JSON vs expected schema. Will provide mockups by 2026-03-12.

2026-03-08 - Diego Morales: Ran a simulated rollout against v1.55 with tokenizer change and observed fidelity drop of 12 points in 10k samples; auto-rollback rule fired in test harness and rollback action created a PR to pin model version. Adjusted threshold to reduce false positives after discussion.

2026-03-10 - Security (Luca Moretti): Reviewed for data leakage risks; confirmed fidelity vectors contain only structural metadata (no user content) and recommended documenting this explicitly for audits. Marking security_review_required=false.
notes_for_release: Feature initially opt-in via feature flag; enable for internal canaries only. Include migration notes for rollout policy editors and a toggle in Console to disable auto-rollback per-customer.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: false positives from overly strict schema rules. Mitigation: fuzz-tuned matcher and configurable per-field tolerance levels.
Risk: performance overhead in hot path. Mitigation: native scorer with sampling mode and p95-optimized path that emits only aggregated signals when sampling disabled.
Risk: alert fatigue. Mitigation: combine fidelity drop with quality eval regression signal before auto-rollback for customer-tiered policies.
